roster.name: Mega Gengar
roster.rationale: Mega Gengar is the premier first-pick cornerstone: Shadow Tag locks both foes in doubles for free KOs, traps, or setup while its 170 SpA / 130 Spe baseline threatens everything under the sun (or rain). At 18 it leaves ample budget for complementary pieces without locking me into a single weather or hyper-offense shell. The name leans into the ability that defines the pick and the closed-door control identity I want the roster to project.

roster.name: Grimmsnarl
roster.rationale: Top Intimidate and redirect options are gone, so Grimmsnarl is the best remaining glue: Prankster Fake Out, Thunder Wave, Light Screen/Reflect, Parting Shot, and Spirit Break give Mega Gengar the speed control and disruption it needs while covering Dark/Fairy roles. At 16 it fits the 18-point ceiling and leaves 66 for eight flexible picks without forcing a second Ghost early. Physical breakers and weather answers remain plentiful next.

roster.name: Annihilape
roster.rationale: Annihilape is the premier physical breaker that thrives under Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag, enabling safe Rage Fist setups and Defiant boosts while covering Fighting needs and adding bulk/priority options. At 14 it fits the budget perfectly and avoids overcommitting points early with 8 slots left. Ghost overlap is manageable given its unique role versus pure Ghost wincons.

roster.name: Maushold
roster.rationale: Maushold at 16 is the cleanest FO redundancy left after Dragapult/Rotom-W went, pairing with Grimmsnarl for dual redirection that enables Shadow Tag Gengar traps and safe Rage Fist ramps on Annihilape while Friend Guard + Tidy Up/Population Bomb add bulk support and a secondary wincon. It fits the 17-point cap perfectly and leaves 36 for six more flexible pieces (Talonflame Tailwind, Water answer, Volcarona/Ceruledge, value Megas). Avoids stacking more Ghosts and shores up the core's biggest immediate hole.

roster.name: Talonflame
roster.rationale: Talonflame at 15 fits the budget perfectly and supplies the Tailwind/Gale Wings speed control my slow-support core desperately needs to enable Mega Gengar traps, Annihilape Rage Fist, and Maushold Tidy Up/Population Bomb. It also adds Fire coverage and a solid revenge killer without overlapping roles. Remaining points (21 for 5 picks) still comfortably cover a Water answer and second wincon next.

roster.name: Primarina
roster.rationale: Primarina fills the critical Water answer hole on a roster weak to Water (especially Talonflame) while adding a strong special wincon and Fairy STAB that synergizes with Grimmsnarl screens and Mega Gengar pressure. At 15 it leaves exactly 6 points for the final 4 picks, which is tight but fillable with value 1-2 cost utility. Higher-cost alternatives like Mega Blastoise lock the remaining budget too hard and Volcarona is already gone.

roster.name: Gliscor
roster.rationale: At 3 points Gliscor is the highest-value glue left that still leaves 3 for three 1-cost fillers: Poison Heal + Toxic Orb bulk, Ground/Flying typing, and Hyper Cutter give me a durable pivot that resists Electric and Ground pressure while checking several common physical threats. It pairs cleanly with Shadow Tag Gengar, Friend Guard Maushold, and Prankster Grimmsnarl without stacking more Ghost/Dark weaknesses. Remaining board still has enough 1-cost utility (Absol, Forretress, etc.) to finish the roster.

roster.name: Forretress
roster.rationale: With a hard 1-pt cap and three slots left, Forretress is the best remaining glue: Sturdy lead, Stealth Rock/Spikes/Toxic Spikes, Rapid Spin, and Volt Switch on a Bug/Steel shell that patches Fairy/Ice/Dragon answers without stacking more Ghost/Dark. Absol’s Super Luck Sucker Punch is a fine breaker but less unique next to Talonflame priority and Grimmsnarl support. Hazards plus a slow pivot improve Mega Gengar/Annihilape/Maushold pressure for the rest of the draft.

roster.name: Altaria
roster.rationale: Cloud Nine Altaria is the highest-value 1-pt glue left: it blanks opposing weather (CharY/Pelipper/TTar/Ninetales cores still out) while adding Dragon/Flying coverage, Tailwind/Roost/EQ/Flamethrower utility and a Natural Cure pivot that doesn't stack more Ghost/Dark. Absol/Banette overlap my existing dark/ghost attackers too hard and Avalugg is a pure physical wall I already approximate with Forretress+Gliscor.

roster.name: Avalugg
roster.rationale: Absol is gone, so Avalugg is the best remaining 1-pt filler: a massive physical wall with Recover, Body Press, and Ice coverage that shores up Fighting-type pressure and gives the team another glue piece alongside Gliscor/Forretress. Banette overlaps Ghost utility with Mega Gengar and is less reliable bulk, while other 1-pts are mostly redundant attackers. Locks a sturdy, low-maintenance final slot for matchup-dependent 6s.

roster.name: Mega Floette
roster.rationale: Mega Floette is the highest-ceiling piece on the board: 155/148 special stats behind Fairy Aura, which turns Moonblast into a spread-safe nuke and Light of Ruin (140 BP x1.33 STAB) into a missile that can OHKO 130-Def Steel/Dragons like Archaludon. Fairy typing plus 148 SpD blanks the Dragon, Dark and Fighting cores that dominate this board, and Fairy Aura also boosts any Fairy partner I add later. There is no replacement for it, whereas Incineroar-style glue (Arcanine, Kangaskhan, Krookodile, Gyarados) can be sourced cheaply in the mid-rounds.

roster.name: Gholdengo
roster.rationale: Gholdengo is the best remaining piece that also patches Mega Floette's exact holes: Steel/Ghost resists Steel and is immune to Poison, the two types that wall Fairy Aura Moonblast, while Floette answers the Dark and Fairy threats that beat Gholdengo. Good as Gold blanks the status-move economy of this board (Whimsicott/Grimmsnarl Prankster, Incineroar Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, Taunt) and Ghost typing dodges Fake Out and Mega Gengar's Shadow Tag trapping, which matters against three drafted rosters. At 16 it's premium value with Nasty Plot/Make It Rain/Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Recover flexibility, and I still have picks 18 and beyond to buy the cheap glue.

roster.name: Sinistcha
roster.rationale: Sinistcha is the scarcest role piece left: Rage Powder to bodyguard Mega Floette, plus Trick Room, Strength Sap (halves incoming physical attackers), Life Dew, Hospitality healing and spread Matcha Gotcha, all on a Ghost type that is immune to Incineroar/Kangaskhan Fake Out. It answers my two biggest holes at once (redirection glue and an alternate speed-control mode) and its Grass/Ghost bulk with 106 Def walls the Ground/Water/Electric attacks that pressure Gholdengo. With a 12-pick gap before my next turn, premium support like this disappears while Tailwind users (Talonflame, Corviknight, Noivern) and Intimidate bodies (Arcanine, Gyarados, Krookodile, Staraptor) stay plentiful and cheap.

roster.name: Tyranitar
roster.rationale: My whole roster is special-attacking and shares Fire/Ghost/Dark weaknesses; Tyranitar resists all three, adds the physical wallbreaker I completely lack, and at 61 Speed it's ideal under Sinistcha's Trick Room. Sand Stream is real weather control against the two rain teams (Pelipper, Politoed) and Mega Charizard Y's Drought, while Unnerve is available when I don't want chip on Floette/Sinistcha. Rock Slide/Knock Off/Ice Punch/Icy Wind plus Assault Vest bulk also walls the Mega Gengar, Dragapult, Delphox and Volcarona-style special threats, and my Ghost/Fairy core covers its 4x Fighting weakness (Sneasler, Annihilape hit nothing).

roster.name: Rotom-Heat
roster.rationale: My core (Floette/Gholdengo/Sinistcha/Tyranitar) is badly exposed to Fire — five of the seven rival rosters already hold Charizard Y, Incineroar, H-Arcanine, Chandelure or Mega Delphox, and both my Ghosts fold to it — while also wanting a Steel answer for Mega Metagross/Kingambit. Rotom-Heat is the only body left that resists Fire, Steel and Fairy at once, is Ground-immune via Levitate, and eats a sun-boosted Heat Wave (15-44%) while Overheat likely OHKOes Metagross. It also gives me the physical glue I lack (Will-O-Wisp, Thunder Wave), a Volt Switch pivot, and Thunderbolt for the Pelipper/Politoed/Gyarados/Basculegion rain shells, all for 12 so I keep 20 points across five slots.

roster.name: Excadrill
roster.rationale: My Tyranitar already turns on permanent sand, which shuts off Zard-Y sun, Pelipper/Politoed rain, and Snow — and Sand Rush Excadrill is the payoff, hitting ~280 raw Speed in sand for real non-Trick-Room speed control I currently lack. It also fixes my biggest coverage hole: I had zero Ground and no physical breaker for the Steel wall (Archaludon, Mega Metagross, Kingambit, Gholdengo, Klefki, Tinkaton) and Fairies my Floette/Sinistcha core struggles to muscle through. Mid-tier is being stripped fast while cheap Intimidate/Fake Out (Mawile 2) and backup Trick Room (Musharna/Mr. Rime 3, Cofagrigus 5) will certainly survive to picks 50/63/66/79, so I spend now and take glue late.

roster.name: Mr. Rime
roster.rationale: Tool check killed my old note: Mawile does not learn Fake Out, so it was just a slow frail Intimidate body. Mr. Rime at 3 gives me everything I actually lack in one slot — Trick Room backup so Sinistcha isn't a single point of failure, plus Fake Out, Icy Wind, Ally Switch, Helping Hand, screens and Freeze-Dry/Triple Axel coverage for the Garchomp/Gliscor/Noivern/Dragapult/Dragonite spam on the other rosters. Taking it now rather than at 63 because it's the single best cheap glue piece left and I have 12 picks of exposure before my next turn, and 3 points still leaves 4 for three fillers.

roster.name: Qwilfish
roster.rationale: My roster has zero Intimidate and a glaring Water weakness (Tyranitar, Excadrill, Rotom-Heat) with two rain cores drafted (Pelipper/Archaludon/Gyarados and Politoed/Basculegion). Qwilfish is the cheapest body that compresses Intimidate, a Water resist, and Poison-type Fighting/Fairy resistance for Sneasler, Annihilape, Mega Medicham and Mega Gardevoir. It also brings Haze, Taunt, Thunder Wave, Icy Wind and Flip Turn, and Swift Swim lets it flip the opponent's own rain into speed control for 2 points.

roster.name: Pidgeot
roster.rationale: My whole roster is slow (TTar 61, Sinistcha 70, Gholdengo 84, Excadrill 88) and my only speed modes are Trick Room and sand-boosted Excadrill; Pidgeot is the only 1-point body left with real Tailwind, giving me a third, opposite gameplan against fast rosters like Dragapult/Aerodactyl/Sneasler/Whimsicott. It also brings U-turn pivoting, Roost, Feather Dance to blunt Kingambit/Sneasler/Metagross physical attackers, and a Ground immunity that pairs with my Ground-weak TTar/Excadrill core. Fake Out duty is already covered by Mr. Rime, so speed control was the bigger hole at this price.

roster.name: Lopunny
roster.rationale: With only 1 point, Lopunny is the most functional support body left: Fake Out, Encore, Helping Hand, After You, Healing Wish, Switcheroo and Thunder Wave off 105 base Speed, with Limber to shrug off paralysis from the many Prankster/Nuzzle users on other rosters. It gives me a second Fake Out beyond Mr. Rime so I can pressure setup leads (Sneasler, Volcarona, Dragonite) without committing my Trick Room piece, and After You/Helping Hand turn Mega Floette and Rotom-Heat into immediate nukes on non-TR turns. Emolga's Motor Drive was the alternative, but Fake Out plus Encore plus Healing Wish is far more flexible across all eight matchups.

roster.name: Mega Charizard Y
roster.rationale: Mega Charizard Y is a premier VGC centerpiece with its monstrous base 159 Special Attack and instant field-warping Drought ability. Its high-velocity Heat Wave spread pressure forces immediate respect from opposing team builds while granting immense weather control against Rain and Snow teams. Taking Charizard-Y first establishes an aggressive, flexible cornerstone that dictates opponent positioning from game one.

roster.name: Venusaur
roster.rationale: Venusaur is the premier Chlorophyll abuser alongside Mega Charizard Y, providing immediate double-speed pressure under Drought. Its Grass/Poison typing perfectly covers Charizard's weaknesses to Water, Rock, and Electric types while giving us fast Sleep Powder, Earth Power, and Fire Weather Ball coverage. At 13 points, it secures our primary offensive Sun core while leaving 67 points for our remaining 8 slots.

roster.name: Tinkaton
roster.rationale: Tinkaton provides our Sun core with premier Steel/Fairy defensive typing, immune to Dragon and Poison while resisting the Rock, Ice, Flying, and Psychic attacks that threaten Mega Charizard Y and Venusaur. Its stellar support movepool—featuring Fake Out, Feint, Knock Off, Helping Hand, and Quash—protects Charizard Y on turn one and allows spread Heat Waves to punish Protect usage. Securing an elite Steel/Fairy pivot at 11 points leaves 56 points for our final 7 slots, keeping budget flexible for Intimidate, a bulky Water anchor, and secondary speed control.

roster.name: Dragapult
roster.rationale: Dragapult provides elite 142 Speed tier, fast U-turn pivot control, and Will-O-Wisp/Breaking Swipe support while complementing Charizard Y, Venusaur, and Tinkaton with key Normal, Fighting, Fire, Grass, and Electric immunities/resistances. Clear Body and Infiltrator allow it to bypass Intimidate, Icy Wind drops, and screens to pressure opposing offensive cores cleanly. Spending 14 points leaves 42 points for 6 picks (7.0 avg/slot), perfectly preserving budget for Ground and Water anchors.

roster.name: Swampert
roster.rationale: Swampert provides essential Water/Ground typing to anchor our defense with a crucial Electric immunity and Rock resistance for Mega Charizard Y, while Charizard and Venusaur eliminate Grass-type threats. At 6 points, Swampert offers excellent physical bulk, Ground STAB unaffected by Sun, slow positioning via Flip Turn, and critical spread protection through Wide Guard. This leaves us with a healthy 36 points for our final 5 picks to flesh out physical disruption and utility.

roster.name: Scrafty
roster.rationale: Scrafty fills critical roster gaps by providing our team's first Fake Out user and Intimidate pivot while adding Dark/Fighting offensive coverage to check opposing Ghost, Dark, Rock, and Steel types. Its impressive 65/115/115 bulk alongside high-value support tools like Coaching, Snarl, Knock Off, and Quick Guard perfectly enables both our Sun core and physical sweepers. At just 3 points, this pick leaves us with 33 points for our final 4 picks to comfortably target prime Trick Room counters and redirection utility.

roster.name: Clefable
roster.rationale: Clefable supplies vital Follow Me redirection support to preserve Mega Charizard Y and Dragapult while offering versatile defense via Unaware against setup sweepers or Magic Guard against passive damage. Its deep utility pool with Helping Hand, Thunder Wave, Healing Wish, and icy coverage patches our control gaps without compromising offensive momentum. Spending 15 points here leaves 18 points across 3 remaining picks, comfortably funding low-cost defensive staples like Garganacl and Skeledirge.

roster.name: Garganacl
roster.rationale: Garganacl gives our team a critical Wide Guard user to shield Mega Charizard Y and Dragapult from Rock Slide and high-damaging spread attacks, while providing an unshakeable Trick Room anchor with Salt Cure and Recover. Purifying Salt makes it immune to status conditions and resists Ghost, giving us a second defensive backbone alongside Clefable. Spending just 5 points keeps 13 points intact to comfortably draft two flexible pieces in our final picks.

roster.name: Skeledirge
roster.rationale: Skeledirge (5 pts) adds a premier Unaware physical wall, Ghost typing for Fake Out immunity, Torch Song snowballing under Drought, and burn support via Will-O-Wisp. With Prankster's Paradise holding 6 points, Skeledirge is a sniper target if left open. Meanwhile, Hisuian Goodra (6 pts) is mathematically guaranteed to wheel back to us at Pick 80 because no opponent behind us has more than 5 usable points for a single pick.

roster.name: Hisuian Goodra
roster.rationale: Hisuian Goodra completes our roster as an elite special tank with an exceptional Steel/Dragon defensive typing. Sap Sipper gives our team an essential Grass immunity and Spore absorber to keep Swampert and Garganacl safe, while its immense bulk and wide coverage complement our sun offense and dual Unaware defensive foundation. Drafting Goodra-Hisui locks in our final 10-Pokémon roster with full positional coverage and match-up flexibility across the board.

Clear Body and Infiltrator allow it to bypass Intimidate, Icy Wind drops, and screens to pressure opposing offensive cores cleanly. Spending 14 points leaves 42 points for 6 picks (7.0 avg/slot), perfectly preserving budget for Ground and Water anchors.

draftRoster.name: Swampert
draftRoster.rationale: Swampert provides essential Water/Ground typing to anchor our defense with a crucial Electric immunity and Rock resistance for Mega Charizard Y, while Charizard and Venusaur eliminate Grass-type threats. At 6 points, Swampert offers excellent physical bulk, Ground STAB unaffected by Sun, slow positioning via Flip Turn, and critical spread protection through Wide Guard. This leaves us with a healthy 36 points for our final 5 picks to flesh out physical disruption and utility.

draftRoster.name: Scrafty
draftRoster.rationale: Scrafty fills critical roster gaps by providing our team's first Fake Out user and Intimidate pivot while adding Dark/Fighting offensive coverage to check opposing Ghost, Dark, Rock, and Steel types. Its impressive 65/115/115 bulk alongside high-value support tools like Coaching, Snarl, Knock Off, and Quick Guard perfectly enables both our Sun core and physical sweepers. At just 3 points, this pick leaves us with 33 points for our final 4 picks to comfortably target prime Trick Room counters and redirection utility.

draftRoster.name: Clefable
draftRoster.rationale: Clefable supplies vital Follow Me redirection support to preserve Mega Charizard Y and Dragapult while offering versatile defense via Unaware against setup sweepers or Magic Guard against passive damage. Its deep utility pool with Helping Hand, Thunder Wave, Healing Wish, and icy coverage patches our control gaps without compromising offensive momentum. Spending 15 points here leaves 18 points across 3 remaining picks, comfortably funding low-cost defensive staples like Garganacl and Skeledirge.

draftRoster.name: Garganacl
draftRoster.rationale: Garganacl gives our team a critical Wide Guard user to shield Mega Charizard Y and Dragapult from Rock Slide and high-damaging spread attacks, while providing an unshakeable Trick Room anchor with Salt Cure and Recover. Purifying Salt makes it immune to status conditions and resists Ghost, giving us a second defensive backbone alongside Clefable. Spending just 5 points keeps 13 points intact to comfortably draft two flexible pieces in our final picks.

draftRoster.name: Skeledirge
draftRoster.rationale: Skeledirge (5 pts) adds a premier Unaware physical wall, Ghost typing for Fake Out immunity, Torch Song snowballing under Drought, and burn support via Will-O-Wisp. With Prankster's Paradise holding 6 points, Skeledirge is a sniper target if left open. Meanwhile, Hisuian Goodra (6 pts) is mathematically guaranteed to wheel back to us at Pick 80 because no opponent behind us has more than 5 usable points for a single pick.

draftRoster.name: Hisuian Goodra
draftRoster.rationale: Hisuian Goodra completes our roster as an elite special tank with an exceptional Steel/Dragon defensive typing. Sap Sipper gives our team an essential Grass immunity and Spore absorber to keep Swampert and Garganacl safe, while its immense bulk and wide coverage complement our sun offense and dual Unaware defensive foundation. Drafting Goodra-Hisui locks in our final 10-Pokémon roster with full positional coverage and match-up flexibility across the board.

roster.name: Archaludon

roster.name: Pelipper

It also covers my critical lack of a Flying-type partner and provides a second bulky support body.

roster.name: Gyarados
roster.rationale: Gyarados gives us the Intimidate support our Archaludon/Pelipper core desperately needs against physical threats like Kingambit, Sneasler, and Mega Metagross. roster.name: Aegislash
roster.rationale: Aegislash (14) is the exact Fairy/Fire check our note called for, giving Steel/Ghost defensive pivoting that pairs well with Archaludon and Pelipper. roster.name: Mega Medicham

roster.name: Incineroar
roster.rationale: Incineroar is the best season-long glue on the board: Intimidate + Fake Out + Parting Shot + Snarl/Will-O-Wisp/Taunt/Helping Hand fits literally every 6 I'll build, and its Fire/Dark typing resists both of Charizard Y's STABs while threatening Mega Gengar. I passed on Sneasler because a 4x Psychic weakness is a liability with Gardevoir/Delphox/Metagross/Alakazam Megas all in the pool. At 18 I keep 82 points for 9 picks, enough for a premium Mega plus support.

roster.name: Mega Metagross
roster.rationale: Mega Metagross is the best remaining mega anchor and a classic Incineroar partner: Intimidate + Fake Out buys it room, and Tough Claws Iron Head/Zen Headbutt threaten huge chunks of the opposing field — it resists Floette's Fairy STAB (Iron Head is a possible OHKO), guaranteed-OHKOs Sneasler 4x with Zen Headbutt, and outspeeds Garchomp, Charizard Y, Archaludon, and Kingambit at base 110. With 8 picks before my next turn, a premium mega like this won't come back around, whereas speed control and Ground/Water coverage have many mid-cost options. Its Ghost/Dark weaknesses are already partially covered by Incineroar, and I can add a dedicated Gengar check cheaply later.

roster.name: Aerodactyl
roster.rationale: Aerodactyl compresses my two most urgent needs into one slot: elite speed control (130 Spe Tailwind + Taunt) and a hard Charizard Y answer (STAB Rock Slide into a 4x weakness, plus Wide Guard to blank Heat Wave for both my slots). Wide Guard also shields Metagross from Earthquake and opposing Rock Slides, which is premium in doubles. Talonflame was the alternative, but it loses to Charizard Y outright and stacks Water/Rock weaknesses with Incineroar; with two rain rosters and a sun roster in the league, Aerodactyl's coverage matters more than Gale Wings priority. Deepseek's slow Kingambit/Farigiraf core makes speed control a likely target for them at pick 23, so I secure it now rather than risk settling for Noivern/Klefki later.

roster.name: Rotom-Wash
roster.rationale: Rotom-Wash is my top-priority target and the most contested piece left on the board — with two rain teams in the league (inkling's Pelipper/Gyarados, gpt's Politoed/Basculegion) and inkling picking right behind me at 29, waiting until pick 37 risks losing it. Levitate makes it a Ground-immune pivot next to Ground-weak Metagross, Thunderbolt deletes Pelipper/Gyarados/Basculegion, and Will-O-Wisp/Thunder Wave/Electroweb give me speed control and physical-attacker answers (Garchomp, Kingambit, Sneasler). It also patches my roster's Water weakness, since Incineroar and Aerodactyl are both Water-weak. At 14 I stay on budget: 34 left for 6 picks keeps Mamoswine + Spiritomb + a speed-control piece affordable.

roster.name: Mamoswine
roster.rationale: Mamoswine is my top remaining need and the most contested piece on my list — deepseek (36 pts) picks twice before my next turn and could easily want it. Ground STAB (Earthquake/High Horsepower) covers Gholdengo, Tinkaton, Archaludon, and Kingambit, while Ice Shard answers Garchomp, Zard Y, and Dragapult; Freeze-Dry is a nice bonus into the rain cores. Learnset confirms everything I need, and at 12 it fits the budget line: 22 left for 5 picks still affords Spiritomb + Klefki + three cheap fillers.

roster.name: Spiritomb
roster.rationale: Spiritomb is my designated Mega Gengar answer: as a Ghost-type it ignores Shadow Tag, resists Gengar's Poison STAB, and threatens back with Dark STAB while packing Snarl, Taunt, Will-O-Wisp, Foul Play, Sucker Punch, and Trick Room (all confirmed). At 6 points it's a bargain utility piece that also blanks Prankster status from Whimsicott and gives me a Trick Room mode or anti-Trick Room Taunt depending on the matchup. It leaves me 16 points for 4 slots, exactly on plan for Noivern plus cheap fillers.

roster.name: Liepard
roster.rationale: Noivern is gone, so I take the best remaining disruption piece before Prankster's Paradise (picking twice before my next turn, theme fit) can snag it. Liepard compresses my biggest needs: Prankster Thunder Wave/Encore/Taunt/Yawn as speed control #2 behind Aerodactyl's Tailwind, a second Fake Out next to Incineroar, and Sunny Day/Rain Dance for weather wars against the Pelipper and Politoed rosters. Its Dark typing makes it immune to opposing Prankster status (Whimsicott, Grimmsnarl, Klefki all drafted) and immune to Psychic, while Copycat can steal enemy Tailwinds/Trick Rooms. At 8 points it leaves exactly 8 for Serperior (5) + Pikachu (1) + Qwilfish-or-Tauros (2).

roster.name: Serperior
roster.rationale: Serperior is still on the board at 5 and fills my biggest gaps exactly as planned: Glare paralyzes Ground-types (Garchomp, Excadrill) that Liepard's Thunder Wave can't touch, and Contrary Leaf Storm gives me a self-boosting special win-con that shreds the Water/Ground stacks and rain cores on Stalwart Steelworks and Prankster's Paradise. The learnset confirms everything I need is legal — Glare, Leaf Storm, Taunt, Knock Off, dual screens, Gastro Acid, and Grassy Glide for priority — and 113 base Speed lets it outrun and Taunt most support pieces. At 5 points it leaves me exactly 3 for my final two picks, keeping the Pikachu + Qwilfish endgame intact.

roster.name: Manectric
roster.rationale: Qwilfish and Absol are gone, so I pivot to the best 1-pointer on the board: Manectric gives Lightning Rod to shield Aerodactyl/Serperior and blank Rotom-Heat/Rotom-Mow/Mega Ampharos, plus real offense at 105 Spe/105 SpA with Thunderbolt, Volt Switch, Snarl (into the league's many special nukes: M-Gardevoir, M-Delphox, M-Gengar, M-Floette), Thunder Wave, and Overheat. Snipe risk matters: King's Gambit has exactly 2 points for 2 slots, so they must buy two 1-pointers before pick 76 — 1-pointers are far likelier to disappear than my 2-point targets (Mawile/Rotom-Fan), which the 5-6 point teams are unlikely to bother with. Spending 1 now locks the scarce resource and leaves 2 points for the final pick.

It also gives a second Intimidate alongside Incineroar plus deep utility — Sucker Punch priority, Knock Off, Taunt, Rock Slide, Helping Hand, Icy Wind, Charm — so it slots into multiple 6-of-10 builds as a glue piece rather than a one-trick.

draftRoster.name: Dragonite
draftRoster.rationale: We have zero Tailwind and no Extreme Speed priority. Dragonite 14 gives Multiscale bulk, Tailwind, and ESpeed in one slot, fixing speed control vs Whimsicott/Talonflame/Noivern teams and checking opposing Dragons, Gengar, and Delphox. At 14 it leaves 11 points for 3 cheap role players to finish Steel + Ghost wall needs.

draftRoster.name: Houndstone
draftRoster.rationale: Need a physical Ghost wall for Kingambit/Maushold/Annihilape and contact attackers. Houndstone 6 gives Fluffy + Wisp + Normal immunity, pairs with Arcanine Intimidate and Klefki screens. Leaves 5 points for 2 picks which perfectly fits Aggron 2 + Passimian/Skarmory 3.

draftRoster.name: Aggron
draftRoster.rationale: With 5 points for 2 picks we must stay <=4. Aggron at 2 gives us the Steel/Rock physical tank we lack - Sturdy/Rock Head, Fairy and Ice resist for Floette/Gardevoir and Dragonite matchups, and Head Smash/Heavy Slam. Leaves 3 points for final flex.

draftRoster.name: Passimian
draftRoster.rationale: With 3 points left, Passimian is perfect final flex. Defiant directly punishes the Incineroar, Arcanine-H, and Intimidate cores in the field, and gives us Close Combat + Knock Off + U-turn for Kingambit/Tyranitar/Excadrill/Gholdengo. It stacks with our Dragonite Tailwind and Klefki Prankster support and completes the anti-Intimidate plan.

roster.name: Kingambit
roster.rationale: Kingambit at 17 points is the best remaining anchor in the pool — Supreme Overlord turns it into a devastating late-game win condition that warps opponent decision-making from team preview onward. Its Dark/Steel typing offers crucial Ghost and Psychic resists that the early drafters (Mega Gengar, Mega Floette, Sneasler) will struggle to break. At 17 points I preserve flexibility with 83 left for nine more picks, and I'm not committing to a Mega or weather archetype before seeing how the board develops.

roster.name: Farigiraf
roster.rationale: Farigiraf is the ideal partner for Kingambit: it sets Trick Room to flip Kingambit's low Speed into an advantage, and Armor Tail blocks Fake Out, Prankster Taunt, and Sucker Punch that would otherwise disrupt Swords Dance setup. At 110 SpA with solid 120 HP bulk, it also fills my need for a special attacker and provides a Normal/Psychic typing that doesn't stack weaknesses with Kingambit. At 18 points it's exactly my max spend and won't survive another round with Trick Room-hungry rosters forming.

roster.name: Mega Gardevoir
roster.rationale: Mega Gardevoir is the ideal Mega for your TR core: 165 SpA Pixilate Hyper Voice devastates under Trick Room, and it learns Trick Room itself — giving you the essential second setter behind Farigiraf. At 100 base Speed, it also flexes into a mid-speed mode when TR is countered, and its Fairy typing rounds out your defensive synergy with Kingambit (Steel/Dark) and Farigiraf (Normal/Psychic).

roster.name: Hisuian Arcanine
roster.rationale: Hisuian Arcanine is the best remaining Intimidate pivot after Incineroar and Gyarados were sniped. Fire/Rock typing gives me crucial coverage I lack, and base 90 Speed lets it function both as a mid-speed attacker under TR and as a respectable threat outside it. At 13 points it leaves 36 for six more picks, keeping Hatterene (9) and a fast-mode option well within reach.

roster.name: Hatterene
roster.rationale: Hatterene (9) is the ideal secondary TR abuser/setter at a bargain price. Magic Bounce shuts down Taunt and Spore aimed at my TR mode, while 136 SpA makes it a genuine offensive threat with Expanding Force and Dazzling Gleam. It leaves 27 points for 5 remaining picks — plenty of room to still grab a fast mode and defensive glue. At 9 points it's a high-value snipe risk; I can't risk waiting 12 picks.

roster.name: Noivern
roster.rationale: Noivern (9 pts) is the perfect speed-control piece for this TR-leaning roster: 123 base Speed with Tailwind gives us a fast mode, Infiltrator bypasses Grimmsnarl screens and Aurora Veil, and Flying/Dragon typing adds a crucial Ground immunity for Kingambit and Hisuian Arcanine. At only 9 points it preserves budget — 18 points for 4 remaining picks keeps defensive glue and role-players affordable. 12 picks before our next turn means we can't gamble on it wheeling back.

roster.name: Milotic
roster.rationale: Milotic is the premium defensive Water I need to patch the Water/Ground vulnerabilities on Hisuian Arcanine and Kingambit. Competitive punishes the format's rampant Intimidate (Incineroar, Gyarados, Arcanine all drafted), which directly protects Kingambit's offensive presence. Base 81 Speed is flexible enough to function in both Trick Room and Tailwind modes, and 95/79/125 bulk with Recover gives the team a durable pivot it currently lacks.

roster.name: Tauros
roster.rationale: Tauros (2 pts) brings Ghost immunity via Normal typing, directly patching my 3-Psychic roster's biggest hole. Intimidate stacks with Hisuian Arcanine for devastating double-Intimidate pivoting, and 110 base Speed thrives under Noivern's Tailwind. With Close Combat, Rock Slide, Wild Charge, and Throat Chop it has coverage to hit almost everything, and Raging Bull offers situational screen-breaking utility.

roster.name: Ampharos
roster.rationale: Ampharos (1pt) fills the Electric-coverage gap at 115 SpA and 55 base Speed — slow enough for Trick Room, fast enough to move outside it with a neutral nature. Its movepool includes Volt Switch for pivoting, Dazzling Gleam to stack Fairy pressure alongside Mega Gardevoir, Dragon Pulse, Focus Blast, and Power Gem for coverage. Static provides incidental paralysis value. This is the best 1-pt special attacker available that fits both modes.

roster.name: Toucannon
roster.rationale: Toucannon is the best 1-point fit: it patches the roster's triple Ground weakness (Kingambit, Arcanine-H, Ampharos) with a Flying-type immunity, brings Tailwind redundancy alongside Noivern, and adds Knock Off utility plus Skill Link coverage. Beak Blast's contact-burn mechanic and Encore give it disruptive potential even with modest bulk, and 120 base Attack ensures it isn't passive.

roster.name: Basculegion-Male
roster.rationale: Basculegion-Male gives Whimsicott an immediate physical win condition, with Tailwind enabling fast Adaptability pressure and Swift Swim preserving a potential rain mode. Its strong priority, immunities, and late-game sweeping ability make it difficult to replace later in the draft.

roster.name: Mega Delphox
roster.rationale: Mega Delphox supplies the elite fast special offense the roster lacks, with base 159 Special Attack, base 134 Speed, strong Fire/Psychic coverage, and a valuable Ground immunity through Levitate. It complements Basculegion’s physical pressure and gives Whimsicott a dangerous Tailwind partner without making the team entirely dependent on speed control.

roster.name: Politoed
roster.rationale: Politoed is the remaining affordable Drizzle setter and immediately unlocks Basculegion’s Swift Swim while strengthening its Water pressure. It also adds useful support flexibility without committing every matchup to rain, leaving 32 points for six picks.

roster.name: Tsareena
roster.rationale: Tsareena adds Queenly Majesty priority denial, helping our rain attackers avoid Fake Out and opposing priority while providing strong physical Grass pressure into Water-types. At 11 points it preserves enough budget to secure an efficient Steel and several cheap defensive role players.

roster.name: Metagross
roster.rationale: Metagross is the best affordable sturdy Steel, providing excellent physical bulk, Clear Body, priority, and reliable Fairy/Ice/Rock coverage without consuming our Mega option. At 6 points it leaves 15 for four picks, enough to add cheap Intimidate, Trick Room counterplay, and another flexible attacker.

roster.name: Mega Ampharos
roster.rationale: Mega Ampharos is a high-value alternative Mega that supplies badly needed Electric pressure, excellent special bulk, and a slow 165 Special Attack threat for potential Trick Room matchups. Its Dragon typing and Mold Breaker also broaden our matchup options, while the 4-point cost preserves an 11-point finish across three slots.

roster.name: Mudsdale
roster.rationale: Mudsdale adds the missing physical Ground attacker and gives the roster a durable Trick Room option that complements Mega Ampharos and Politoed. Its Stamina, Inner Focus, and low Speed provide valuable matchup flexibility, while preserving exactly 6 points for the final two slots.

roster.name: Toxicroak
roster.rationale: Toxicroak supplies our missing Fake Out while adding Fighting and Poison pressure, priority, Taunt, Feint, and Coaching options. Dry Skin gives it excellent synergy with Politoed’s rain, and spending 4 preserves exactly 2 points for an Intimidate user with the final pick.

roster.name: Arbok
roster.rationale: Arbok completes the roster with a low-cost Intimidate option, giving the team valuable physical damage mitigation without relying on Mudsdale’s bulk. Its disruptive toolkit and flexible Poison utility complement Whimsicott’s speed control and the rain offense built around Basculegion.

teambuilds.rationale: Our Sun offense core of Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur exerts immense speed and firepower against their roster, outspeeding Sneasler and burning through Klefki, Rotom-Mow, Aggron, and Houndstone. Dragapult natively outspeeds their entire team, using Infiltrator to bypass Klefki screens and Dragon Darts to crack Dragonite Multiscale and Garchomp. Clefable provides Unaware walling and Follow Me redirection against Dragon Dance Dragonite and Swords Dance Garchomp, while Garganacl neutralizes status, Wide Guards Rock Slide / Earthquake, and wears down bulky switch-ins with Salt Cure. Hisuian Goodra with Sap Sipper completely counters Rotom-Mow and absorbs special attacks.

Use Whimsicott Tailwind or Politoed rain to enable Adaptability Basculegion, while Tsareena blocks Dragonite and Sneasler priority. Mega Delphox outspeeds even maximum-Speed Sneasler and pressures the opponent's Poison, Ghost, Grass, and Steel pieces; Metagross supplies an Intimidate-proof physical anchor. Rain weakens Arcanine and Chandelure, while the combined Ice and Ground coverage keeps Garchomp, Dragonite, Klefki, and Aggron from walling the offense.

Stalwart Steelworks relies on rain synergy, fast physical pressure, and boost setup with Archaludon, Pelipper, Volcarona, and Mega Medicham. Mega Charizard Y and Chlorophyll Venusaur take weather control and break their Steel/Water core under Sun. Dual Unaware walls Skeledirge and Clefable shut down Quiver Dance Volcarona while providing Follow Me and Fighting immunities against Mega Medicham. Garganacl uses Wide Guard to block spread attacks and Salt Cure to chip Steel/Water types, with Dragapult providing fast speed control.

Opponent is sun with Mega Charizard Y + Chlorophyll Venusaur plus Dragapult speed. Answer with Tailwind Dragonite to outrun Pult and Venusaur, double Rock Slide from Garchomp/Dragonite for 4x vs Zard Y, Flash Fire Chandelure to absorb sun Fire, Intimidate Arcanine + Will-O-Wisp for Tinkaton/Scrafty/Swampert, Rotom-Mow Levitate core vs Swampert/Garganacl, and Sneasler Fake Out + Unburden Sash to double speed and KO Fairy with Gunk Shot.

We bring Pelipper with Damp Rock to set rain, weakening Charizard Y's sun and fire output. Archaludon and Corviknight form a steel defensive core that resists Dragapult's dragon/ghost and Tinkaton's fairy hits. Aegislash pivots with King's Shield and Shadow Ball to check Skeledirge and Clefable. Mega Medicham delivers a Pure Power-boosted Fighting/Psychic punch to break Garganacl and Goodra-Hisui. Gyarados adds Intimidate and Dragon Dance to pressure Swampert and Scrafty.

Opponent brings rain (Politoed+Basculegion/Toxicroak), fast Tailwind Whimsicott and two fast/slow Megas (Delphox 134, Ampharos 45). Our 6 answers with double Levitate (Rotom-Mow + Dragonite) to blank Mudsdale EQ, Klefki Light Clay screens + Prankster TWave to blunt both Megas and win Prankster war, Arcanine Intimidate + double Will-O-Wisp to cripple Basculegion/Metagross/Mudsdale, Sneasler Unburden Sash Fake Out to stop Whimsicott Taunt (Fake Out +3 > Prankster +1) and fast Poison for Fairy, and Dragonite Tailwind + ESpeed to outspeed Mega Delphox after setup.

Use Whimsicott or rain to establish speed control, with Mega Delphox naturally outrunning even maximum-Speed Mega Gengar and threatening an immediate Psychic KO. Politoed and Swift Swim Basculegion form the fast rain mode, while Tsareena blocks priority and pressures Primarina and Gliscor. Metagross punishes Grimmsnarl screens with Psychic Fangs and supplies durable answers into the opponent's Fairy, Ice, and Poison threats.

We bring Mega Medicham for Pure Power physical pressure, Stunfisk for Earthquake and electric immunity, Volcarona for Quiver Dance sweeping, Corviknight for Tailwind and bulk, Aegislash for Wide Guard and ghost/steel pivoting, and Archaludon for Stamina walling with Rest/Sleep Talk. This covers Mega Metagross with fighting/ground/fire, handles Rotom-Wash and Manectric via Stunfisk, and uses Tailwind to outpace Aerodactyl and Serperior. Wide Guard protects against spread Earthquake and Rock Slide, while Fake Out and King's Shield provide disruption.

Triple Trick Room (Farigiraf/Hatterene/Mega Gardevoir) with Noivern Tailwind for speed flexibility. Armor Tail + Kingambit's Dark typing shut down Grimmsnarl's Prankster entirely; Hatterene's Magic Bounce also reflects status. Kingambit is the dedicated Mega Gengar answer with STAB Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave. Arcanine-H provides Intimidate support and OHKOs Talonflame with Rock Slide. Infiltrator Noivern bypasses screens and sets an alternate fast mode when Trick Room is unfavourable.

Opponent’s likely rain core (Politoed + Swift Swim Basculegion) plus Mega Delphox, Metagross, and Whimsicott is answered by Cloud Nine Altaria shutting weather off on entry while Mega Gengar Shadow Tags and deletes Psychic/Steel/Fairy cores. Grimmsnarl Light Clay screens plus Fake Out blunt their openers and Spirit Break cuts Delphox/Ampharos damage; Avalugg Wide Guard/Body Press walls Metagross, Mudsdale, and physical Basculegion. Annihilape Rage Fist stacks into Metagross/Delphox and Defiant punishes Arbok, while Primarina supplies Water/Fairy spread and Moonblast for Ampharos/Dragon targets.

Dual speed control to handle their sand mode (Excadrill under Sand Rush is threat #1). Farigiraf sets Trick Room to reverse Excadrill's speed advantage; Noivern provides Tailwind as a faster option and is Ground-immune. Kingambit + Mega Gardevoir form the offensive core — Gardevoir's Pixilate Hyper Voice gets boosted by Floette's Fairy Aura, Mystical Fire roasts Gholdengo, and Aura Sphere deletes Tyranitar. Arcanine-H Intimidate weakens their physical attackers. Milotic's Competitive punishes Qwilfish's Intimidate. Farigiraf's Normal typing blanks Gholdengo's Shadow Ball.

Stalwart Steelworks is steel-heavy with a rain core (Pelipper/Gyarados/Archaludon), Mega Medicham as breaker, and Volcarona as win-con. My double-Electric core (Rotom-W + Lightning Rod Manectric) guaranteed-OHKOs both Water/Flyings, blanks Electro Shot/Thunder, and Manectric's 172 Spe outruns their whole roster; Aerodactyl's Tailwind (200 Spe) stacks speed control and Rock Slide deletes Volcarona. The steel backbone (Archaludon/Aegislash/Stunfisk) collapses to Mamoswine and Metagross Earthquakes plus Incineroar's Flare Blitz, while Mega Metagross (216 Atk/178 Spe) outruns and pressures everything. Medicham is defused by Intimidate + Chople on Incineroar, Will-O-Wisp from Rotom, and faster Zen Headbutt/Dual Wingbeat revenge. Main caution: keep Mamoswine and Incineroar away from rain-boosted Waterfall, and hit Corviknight (EQ-immune) with Fire/Electric.

Answer with Choice Scarf Garchomp 253 Speed to KO it, Sneasler Unburden Sitrus to double to 378 after Fake Out pressure, and Shed Shell Arcanine to guarantee Intimidate cycling out of Shadow Tag. Mega Gengar + Prankster screens blunt and trap their offense while Annihilape (Ghost immunity to Fighting, Defiant vs Intimidate) and Primarina (Liquid Voice HV + Moonblast) form the win conditions. Gliscor (Hyper Cutter) and Avalugg (Wide Guard/Recover) answer EQ, physical pressure, and Dragons without overlapping roles.
